h1: Compact hydraulic press brakes — 16 to 66 US tons, 2 to 8 ft
intro: A compact hydraulic press brake bends sheet between a punch and a V-die like its big brothers, at the size that fits a sheet-metal shop rather than a steel-fabrication plant: 2 to 8 ft of bending length and 16 to 66 US tons, on a footprint that goes through a door and runs on a 600 V or 208 V supply. NovoTech sells three on this page: the Dener XL 1560 — the smallest machine of the premium line, 66 US tons over 5 ft with the 15.6″ ESA S840 2D control, Y1-Y2 ram on linear scales, a ball-screw X back gauge and EUROSTAMP tooling in the crate, built in Turkey; NovoTech's own value-line compacts, built to our specification — the WAD-50T CNC brakes, 55 US tons over 4.3 and 5.2 ft with servo valves and a Delem DA-53Tx, and the WC67K-30T torsion-bar NC brake, 33 US tons over 5.2 ft with an Estun E21PS; and the value-line HBV bending brakes, 16 to 35 tons, with a four-way V-block (HBV24 / 48) or two cylinders (HBV-1250 / 2540) for brackets, clips and short parts in plate to 3/16″. For HVAC fittings, enclosures, signage, brackets and job-shop work where a 100-ton machine is more than you need. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For 10 ft and longer, or 1/4″ plate and up, see the hydraulic press brakes; for a brake with no hydraulic oil the electric press brakes.

faq.a: Bending force depends on the sheet thickness, the bend length and the V-die opening: F = S² × 2 × R ÷ (1.4 × V) tonnes per metre with S and V in millimetres and R = 47 kg/mm² for mild steel — in inches and US tons per foot about 575 × t² ÷ V. In a V of 8 × the thickness, a 4 ft bend takes about 16 US tons in 16 ga, 39 tons in 10 ga and 47 tons in 8 ga (0.16″); a wider die lowers the force — 8 ga in a 2″ V takes about 31 tons over 4 ft — at the cost of a larger inside radius. The control calculates the exact force for the tool and material you enter; send us your thickest and longest bend and we size the machine.

faq.q: Dener XL 1560 or a value-line compact?
faq.a: The XL 1560 is the premium machine: the heaviest frame, servo-valve hydraulics, an ESA 2D control with collision control, the DSP-AP laser finger guard as standard, every Dener option open to it — 3D controls, 4- to 6-axis back gauges, CNC crowning, Wila clamping, robot cells — and parts stocked in Canada; it bends 3/16″ over the full 5 ft and 1/4″ over 4 ft. The value-line WAD-50T is the same electro-hydraulic servo architecture (servo valves, linear scales, Delem control) built to our specification at a lower price, for 1/8″ over 5.2 ft; the WC67K-30T is the simple torsion-bar NC brake for one material and repeat parts. If the brake runs all day or you program from CAD, the XL; if it bends brackets and enclosures a few hours a day, the value line.

An NC brake (the WC67K-30T) sets the ram depth and the back gauge from a stored program, with the two cylinders kept in step by a torsion bar — enough for the same parts in one material. A CNC brake (the XL 1560 and the WAD-50T) measures the ram on linear scales and corrects it through servo valves, calculates tonnage, bend sequence and gauge positions from the drawing, and changes material and tool in the program — the machine for mixed work, tight angles and multi-bend parts. The buying guide on the press brake page compares every control these machines are sold with.

faq.q: Press brake or HBV bending brake?
faq.a: The XL 1560, WAD-50T and WC67K-30T are press brakes: a programmable ram, a motorised back gauge, segmented tooling and a guard, for sheet work all day. The HBV is a hydraulic bending brake for short parts in plate — brackets, clips, tabs — bent on a four-way V-block (HBV24 / 48) or between two cylinders (HBV-1250 / 2540) with a hand-wheel back gauge, at a fraction of the price. If you bend panels and enclosures, a press brake; if you bend 3/16″ plate brackets a few at a time, the HBV.

faq.q: What tooling fits, and do you stock it?
faq.a: European-style (Promecam / Amada) segmented tooling fits every line: the premium Dener brakes carry European-style top-tool holders, the value-line brakes their own clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V or 4-V die ships with every machine (a 4-V die with the Dener brakes, a 2-V die with the value line) — tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the holders to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; quick-release, pneumatic and Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options, not standard equipment.

faq.q: Are they safe to run without a separate guarding system?
faq.a: Every compact press brake carries side guards, an enclosed rear guard with interlocked doors and a foot pedal with emergency stop; the Dener XL 1560 comes with the DSP-AP laser finger guard and an MCS safety PLC as standard, and on the value-line machines a laser guard — DSP, Fiessler AKAS or a light curtain — is an option we recommend. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — NovoTech sells, installs and supports press brakes across Canada and the United States. Installation, commissioning and operator training are free of charge in the Greater Toronto Area; outside the GTA our technicians do the same work at an additional charge. Parts are stocked in Canada. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.

faq.q: What does delivery cost, and who unloads the machine?
faq.a: A press brake ordered from the factory (back-ordered) travels in its container straight from the port, customs and the rail yard to your plant door: in the Greater Toronto Area that delivery is free; outside the GTA the freight is quoted and charged. A machine from NovoTech's stock is loaded, shipped and unloaded at the buyer's cost. In every case unloading is the buyer's responsibility and expense — the crane or forklift, the rigging and moving the machine onto its foundation — so book a rigger for the delivery day; we are glad to recommend riggers who know press brakes and to tell you the weight and lifting points.

No — the hydraulic oil is bought by the customer. Before commissioning, fill the tank with ISO VG 46 anti-wear hydraulic oil (AW 46) in the quantity shown in the specification table for your model; our technician checks the level and bleeds the system during installation. Electric press brakes have no hydraulic oil at all.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
